Good Folk Cafe

A downloadable game for Windows and macOS

Download NowName your own price


Good Folk Cafe is in active development! If you wish to support us, follow us on Instagram, join our community on Discord, and wishlist us on Steam!


The Game

Follow Aoife on their journey to reconnect with their past, nature, and ultimately themself. Explore the land, forage for wild plants, craft bespoke dishes, and delight mysterious otherworldly clientele. Along the way, Aoife will learn about the plants around them, the folklore told in the area, and their family's past.


Explore a rugged and wild landscape

Of white roads winding by the edge
Of bare, untamèd land,
Where dry stone wall or ragged hedge
Runs wide on either hand

  • Forage plants along the way. Manage the space in your bag and find the perfect plant for your dish!
  • Identify Plants, learn about the real wild plants of Ireland as you accumulate knowledge in and out of the game.
  • Cook beautiful dishes with the bounty you've gathered on your trails. Take your time assembling bespoke dishes for your mysterious customers.
  • Uncover the past as you interact with your otherworldly neighbours.
  • Rewilding starts within. Join Aoife as they learn to live a simple life in the wilderness. Repair abandoned equipment and decorate your wild camp.
  • Meet the locals, listen to their stories, learn from their tales, and enjoy their company when they visit Aoife for a cuppa.
  • Relax and find stillness in nature.


Development

Created in Ireland with love, Good Folk Cafe is inspired by our own experiences of life in Ireland and the tales that have been shared with us.

We've sung in pubs, listened to tales told by an oral storyteller, tasted plants on our walk in the wilderness and visited spiritual sites.

We've even shown our game to trad musicians, and the live piece they did is featured in our ambience teaser.

Beelim Solutions9 days ago (1 edit) (+1)

The development team is called "Not Here Not There" - and unfortunately, their name is also a very apt description of this game.

WARNING - the writer of this review is a middle-aged, college-educated Asian male, with a strong inclination toward task-based activity and has had a lifelong involvement with history-themed RTS games (as if it wasn't obvious from my multiple projects on itch.io so far). Keep in mind that this bias may have coloured my expectations and perception of this game.

This game may be your cup of tea, if you are already into the foraging lifestyle - and enjoy seeing what you know (of Irish plants I guess) reflected in this game. But I think I will be passing this and waiting for Haunted Chocolatier or Mandrake to drop first. I am aware that this is meant to be a slow, cosy game - but progress is so slow and seemingly imperceptible that it goes from being cosy to simply just numbing.

At the very bare bones of it, Good Folk Cafe is a game where you forage for ingredients and prepare meals for eldritch creatures, who somehow have managed to scrounge human-designed artefacts which we would otherwise consider as junk hardware parts. 

It's got potential but if things stay the same way as the demo shows, it is going to be neither here nor there.

Perhaps this review is very harsh but I see many red flags.

Number one, the loops. 

The gameplay loops might be interesting but so far they feel monotonous and very much same-y. Perhaps it is because this game is still deep in development so this is all you have to work with. The lack of a proper tutorial also leaves some of us in a state somewhat ... disoriented. You are not told how to prepare ingredients - I closed my first night down early without feeding anyone because I did not know that you had to click the fae spirits who are queueing up to feed. Nor are you told, either, that there's a cooking minigame or that you can use items in the cooking interface to prep food further (we expected that this would be done automatically).

Number two, the writing and the UI design.

There's Fran, the Storyteller. I found his recital too long winded and I mostly skipped to the next day (I'm a reader not a listener), thinking I'd just read the transcript of his first story, the "yellow well" but I found it to be so rambling and inconcise that I might have well been reading the freshest word salad ever to be showcased on Booktok. I understand that not everone in real life must be a polished storyteller .... but I thought this was supposed to be a game, after all, not a philological exercise. The worst part was that there was such a massive wall of text against a colour scheme that obscured UI elements, squashed into a column so narrow that reading what Fran said the other night was nearly impossible.

Less difficult to figure out were what the spirits were asking for - but again, this is dangerous. From reading the transcripts of these creatures' chatter - very beautifully written but alas not very informative - I was asking myself many times over, "Does this customer actually want to try something new, or does it actually want a dish it's had before?" I decided to err on the side of caution although it is hard to say if ever at all what effect my approach had on th game especially after seeing what other players had encountered on youTube.

Not Here, Not There9 days ago (1 edit)

Thank you so much for taking the time to write your feedback. The game is still fairly early in development, so it's really useful to understand how you feel about the game. 

- Gameplay loops. Now that we have the overall loop figured out, our plan is to go back to each gameplay loop and make them more interesting and varied. 

- Tutorial. UX is a battle of attrition. We don't want to swarm the player with tutorial boxes, so we are improving step by step. Everytime we get feedback that one part of the game is hard to understand, we iterate on it.  Getting your feedback is really important for that!

- Storytelling. Those stories are not written by us. We went on a trip to Donegal to meet local musicians and storytellers. Fran is an actual Seanachaí - an Irish myth teller - we met, and it's his voice we hear in the game. We just recorded him on the fly as a test for the demo. The final version of the game will be a lot more polished in terms of quality. Having said that, it's a very specific style of storytelling, and we will stay true to that. 

- UI. We are looking for help with both UI and UX. It will be much better in the final game, I promise!

- The Faes being mysterious characters that you'll get to know a bit but will never fully understand is a core part of our theme and, as far as I understand myself, is also a big part of the Irish mythology. 
We want to make the gameplay of trying to guess what type of dish they like as fun as possible.

What would have helped in your case to make that part of the experience more enjoyable?

Beelim Solutions9 days ago

If there was one thing I would change, really change, it would be the pacing.
Rather than have the game move from day to day I'd make it move from week to week, just so that players would then be prompted into understanding that some things in this game are seasonal - it provides faster changes of scenery, and also forces them to put a little more brain power into this game rather than simply just turning it into a simple click fest where one feeding session seems to look too much like the last one at any given point in time. That is just MY opinion, though.

Reply
Not Here, Not There9 days ago

Oh... interesting! We do want the seasons to have a big impact on the game, so going by weeks would solve some of our issues. It would also slow down the pace of the experience (over weeks) without slowing down the pace of the gameplay (the opposite actually since seasons will have an impact on plants) 
We'll munch on this. Thanks!!!

Hello Tsuneko,

Thank you so much for the gameplay video; it's really helpful for us to see the problem. 

So, in the Foraging map, when you forage plants, the bottom part of the inventory is the overflow. It's meant to be used when you have too many plants in your bag, and you want to switch plants. It is discarded when you go back to the Homestay.

Basically, you want to put your plants in the upper part of the inventory.

It's a known issue with the UX of the bag. We will improve it in the future.
